axes.model_access: Canvas nodes connect to each vendor's LLMs/embeddings/vector stores (built on the LangChain component family); provider coverage follows the official docs, not verified item by item.
axes.runtime: Open-source self-hosting (npm/Docker) + official cloud, two lines; GitHub 55,513★ (API-verified 2026-10-21; last push 2026-08-13 — the slowing cadence is a fact, recorded honestly).
axes.local_files: Self-hosted instance data lands in your own environment; chatflow uploaded-file handling happens inside the instance.
axes.background: A continuously running self-hosted instance carries API serving and queues; the official docs provide a queue mode (details not verified item by item).
axes.tools: The node ecosystem includes tools/retrieval/agent flows; MCP support status not verified item by item.
axes.context: Chatflow memory nodes (buffer/window and other LangChain memory components) are the official context surface; cross-app memory not verified item by item.
axes.permissions: Community edition has basic auth; SSO/workspace isolation etc. live in the enterprise directory (commercial-license zone).
axes.fit: Fits: fast starts building LLM apps on a canvas (RAG/agent flows), self-hosting. Does not fit: out-of-the-box enterprise features; an active release cadence (pushes slowed after 2026-08 — dossier-snapshot framing).

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The closest test protocol is the code-side [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md) (the tool-calling and credential-boundary sections are reusable; no workflow-platform-specific protocol exists on this site yet).
unknowns:
- The full provider/node catalog (not verified item by item)
- MCP support status (no official documentation found)
- An official explanation for the slowing release cadence (none found — only repository facts recorded, no guessing at causes)
related: Both LLM canvases: Langflow belongs to DataStax, is MIT repo-wide, and is larger; Flowise came earlier with a mixed license.
